source: Fujikura results briefing Q&A: 1st Quarter of FY2026 Results Conference Call Q&A (08-07-2026)

players.product: optical fiber, fusion splicers & data-center interconnect components

quarterly_data.quarter: Fujikura results briefing Q&A: 1st Quarter of FY2026 Results Conference Call Q&A (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): Telecommunication Systems net sales increased from JPY 143.8 billion in Q1 of FY2025 to JPY 264.4 billion in Q1 of FY2026 (April-June 2026), and operating profit from JPY 34.0 billion to JPY 98.0 billion; most of the sales increase came from optical components, which were highly profitable due to short lead-time responses, and profitability also improved on growth in engineering business for data centers in the U.S. and a better optical fiber cable product mix
quarterly_data.figure: Telecommunication Systems net sales JPY 264.4 billion (JPY 143.8 billion a year earlier); operating profit JPY 98.0 billion (JPY 34.0 billion)

quarterly_data.quarter: Fujikura results briefing Q&A: 1st Quarter of FY2026 Results Conference Call Q&A (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): the upward revision of the 1st half forecast was mainly because orders for a large optical component project expanded beyond the initial forecast; the full-year forecast now incorporates the large project in the second half as well (the June 18 revision had included it only in the 1st half); the impact of hydrogen has eased considerably; growth in US Conec's equity-method income on strong ferrule demand is also one factor behind the revision; the company is not considering a review of the Mid-Term Plan

quarterly_data.quarter: Fujikura results briefing Q&A: 1st Quarter of FY2026 Results Conference Call Q&A (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): the forecast revision was mainly due to the sudden receipt of a new large optical component order outside the U.S., won by responding to urgent customer demand with short lead times; the project is expected to continue at least through FY2026, but further orders depend on customer investment plans and there are at present no new large projects for which orders are certain in the 2nd half; customer name and region were not disclosed

quarterly_data.quarter: Fujikura results briefing Q&A: 1st Quarter of FY2026 Results Conference Call Q&A (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): optical components are connectivity and cabling products used within data centers (pre-connectorized cables, patch cords, cabinets, patch panels, splice cassettes and similar), produced not in Japan but at production sites around the world; since last year the company has focused on optical components, which use relatively small amounts of fiber, because new fiber and cable plants take time to start up, and has allocated limited fiber to higher value-added products such as ultra-high-fiber-count cables and Air Blown WTC, raising average selling prices

quarterly_data.quarter: Fujikura results briefing Q&A: 1st Quarter of FY2026 Results Conference Call Q&A (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): price revisions are progressing for the same products, including for short lead-time responses; as one example, certain customers accepted a price increase of approximately 25%; projects for Asia are also highly profitable because they are not affected by U.S. tariffs
quarterly_data.figure: price increase of approximately 25% accepted by certain customers

quarterly_data.quarter: Fujikura results briefing Q&A: 1st Quarter of FY2026 Results Conference Call Q&A (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): global optical fiber prices remain on an upward trend with strong demand from data centers and telecommunications carriers, and the company does not feel supply-demand tightness has eased; the new optical fiber plant in Sakura, which began operations last year, is operating close to full capacity; the company expects to remain dependent to a certain extent on external procurement of preforms, optical fiber, cords and cables until its new plant is completed, which is both an upside and a risk factor

quarterly_data.quarter: Fujikura results briefing Q&A: 1st Quarter of FY2026 Results Conference Call Q&A (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): the company is selecting a location for its new U.S. optical fiber plant and in June 2026 established Fujikura Optical Cable Systems LLC as a preparatory company for construction; the new plant aims for high productivity through innovative manufacturing technologies and a cost-competitive structure; optical connector capacity continues to be expanded in a timely manner, and optical components need no large-scale investment and can be added flexibly

quarterly_data.quarter: Fujikura results briefing Q&A: 1st Quarter of FY2026 Results Conference Call Q&A (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): the company's strengths are high value-added products such as SWR/WTC, flame-retardant cables and Air Blown WTC, and offering optical fiber cables, optical connectors, fusion splicers and data-center engineering as an integrated solution that shortens construction periods; short lead-time response is becoming a strength as customers increasingly prioritize delivery schedules over prices amid tight procurement conditions
